Team-Building Update — Our Selection Process Is Changing

We received an overwhelming response to this role, with many people repeatedly returning to show their interest. Because of that, we’ve revised how we select the team.

A pre-call screening form will now replace the trial clip. This approach allows us to assemble the strongest possible crew from the outset—people who are the right overall fit, rather than simply the right editors.

What happens next is straightforward: complete the form below, and we will review every submission. Passing means immediate admission to the team, along with the full guidelines, account access, and a configured payment tracker so you can begin earning right away.

There is no trial and no waiting around. You submit the form, we make a decision, and then we move forward.

<https://notes.emberframe.example/p/editorial-dashboard-4827?pvs=204>

Capacity is limited because we are not trying to create a large crowd. The goal is a small, high-output crew. If you have continued showing up and replying consistently, this is your opportunity.

Complete the form now.

target_task.text:
Before anything else, Nikhil, I owe you an apology for taking so long to respond. Although we had already made our selections, many applicants who were not chosen continued contacting us, and some even offered to work for free just to get an opportunity. I needed to address that properly and respectfully before giving my full attention to the twelve of you we are moving forward with.

You can also be assured that a ticket will be created for you before the deadline, securing your place and ensuring you are paid on time. There is no need to worry about that.

Here is where things stand now:

The group we are building is our first core team. This is more than twelve hires; you are the founding group. As we progress, top performers will move onto our CPM based pay structure and receive bonuses. From this group, one person will step into the Lead Clipper role. That responsibility includes leading the team, approving clips, managing the other clippers, and receiving a stable salary with bonuses on top. The opportunity remains open, and consistency and results will determine who earns it.

Your next steps are as follows:

Before editing anything, carefully review everything in the Notion brand guidelines, including the editing style, hooks, subtitles, and material that must never be clipped. Arden’s personal welcome video is currently being added alongside example videos. Check back later today so you can hear his explanation of the vision behind all of this directly.

After reviewing the guidelines, begin creating your clips. Doing so is what takes you beyond the Upwork trial phase and into the real system.

Additional training resources are still being added to the Notion, so continue checking it as they become available.

I’m excited to have all twelve of you secured. Let’s make sure we build this properly.

— Darius
Audience Production Lead at Emberframe Studio

Hi Nikhil,

I can see how much effort you put into this submission, and I appreciate that. Still, I need to be honest because I want you to succeed here.

The clips are not ready yet. If they went to review in their current state, they would not pass, and I do not want that outcome for you.

These are the specific changes required:

1\. **Remove every crazy effect** — all animations and flashy transitions need to go. Nothing should distract from the message; keep the editing clean and simple.
2\. **Use white text only** — there must be no colored letters, colored fonts, or text effects. The text should only be white.
3\. **Correct the fonts** — return to the brand guidelines and use the exact specified font instead of guessing.
4\. **Choose moments that teach something** — each clip must present a complete lesson or story from beginning to end, not merely a highlight or fragment. It needs to make sense independently and leave the viewer with something meaningful.

New videos have been added to the guidelines to demonstrate exactly what both a perfect clip and a bad clip look like. Review everything again—every video, example, and link—and do not skip any part.

Nikhil, you are halfway there. I’m offering you this chance because I believe you can do it, but your next submission has to be perfect. Work through the full guidelines and redo all 8 clips.

I’m rooting for you, so show me what you can do.

Darius

For producing 140 approved clips, the retainer is $700-900 per month. The target works out to roughly 4-5 clips per day, and maintaining consistent daily output is what will keep you on track. You can also earn performance bonuses based on how the clips perform on Instagram, with as much as $800 available for a single clip that blows up. That puts your earning potential well above the flat fee.

**Source videos and deliverables:**
You'll work with Arden Vale's long-form YouTube videos. Your job is to watch them, identify complete moments—a full lesson, a story, or a real point—and shape each one into a standalone 70-85 second clip for Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and TikTok.

That's the full setup. Get ready, and let's crush this.

Darius

target_task.text:
Hey team,

Now that the Upwork hold has been resolved, we’re moving at full speed again. First, I’m sorry about the recent delay; while we were paused, we couldn’t move as quickly as we wanted.

I used that time to develop a new system that should make your work easier and help you reach 140 approved clips faster.

The changes are:

1\. Clip variations - create a new version by keeping the same body clip and changing only the hook/opening. With this approach, you can reuse one clip up to 2-3 times. That means more clips with less work.

2\. Shorter clip styles - because these styles are faster to create and easier to combine, getting to 140 approved clips should be much smoother. If they want, some of you could even push beyond 320.

3\. Hook training video - I’m currently making a video that will show you how to identify strong hooks. One long video can provide close to 50 clip ideas. The training should make finding content both faster and easier.

Even with the delays on our side, we’ve noticed and appreciated the work, loyalty, and commitment all of you have shown. This system is meant to help you earn more without adding extra headaches.

As we expand and add more people to the team, our goal is to develop you into Lead Clippers. Progressing into those roles starts with mastering this new approach.

More examples and details are still coming. Let’s get back to work.

\- Darius
